decision.summary: Tom Achterberg's email of 10 Oct 2026 gives one month's notice for 10 Nov 2026. Under the Renters' Rights Act 2025 a tenant needs two months' written notice, so the earliest valid end date is 10 Dec 2026, unless the landlord agrees in writing to a shorter period. The tenant has been told this, and the 10 Nov request is with landlord Ben Hartley for decision by 16 Oct 2026, with a follow-up set.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: Not valid as given for 10 Nov. One month is shorter than the two months required of a tenant under the Renters' Rights Act 2025 (in force 1 May 2026). Served 10 Oct 2026, the earliest valid end date is 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only if the landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice period or a different end date (e.g. 10 Nov 2026). The tenant cannot shorten it unilaterally. The request is with the landlord (APR-102). Otherwise the tenancy runs to 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to the tenant (MSG-101) with the 10 Dec 2026 earliest valid end date, that the 10 Nov request is with the landlord, and that key and deposit details follow once the end date is set. Started a landlord decision request (APR-102, deadline 16 Oct 2026) and a dated follow-up (FUP-103). No maintenance ticket exists for P-250, so no ticket hold could be placed.

actions_claimed.description: Sent email to tenant Tom Achterberg explaining the valid notice period and the 10 Dec 2026 earliest end date (MSG-101).
Requested landlord Ben Hartley's decision on early end on 10 Nov 2026 vs 10 Dec 2026 (APR-102).
Scheduled follow-up FUP-103 to chase landlord decision on 16 Oct 2026.

failed_actions.handling: put_on_hold on P-250 failed: no maintenance ticket with that reference exists (a property id, not a ticket). Not retried, as no ticket exists to hold. Replaced with a dated follow-up (FUP-103) for 16 Oct 2026.

assumptions: Notice was served on the date of the email, 10 Oct 2026.
Tenancy is an assured periodic tenancy converted 1 May 2026, per the CRM.
Deposit of £2,019 is within the 5-week cap (£1,750 rent x 5 weeks ~ £2,019).

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for your email, and congratulations on the new job in Manchester.

Your notice has been received. Since 1 May 2026, a tenant on a periodic tenancy needs to give at least two months' written notice. Based on today's date (10 October 2026), the earliest date your tenancy can end under your notice is 10 December 2026. Rent remains payable until the tenancy ends.

If you would like to leave on 10 November, you would need your landlord to agree to the shorter notice in writing. I have passed your request to your landlord, Ben Hartley, and will let you know his answer as soon as we have it. Please don't arrange your move on 10 November until you have heard from us.

Keys: we will confirm the return arrangements with you once the end date is agreed.

Deposit: your deposit of £2,019 is held in the mydeposits scheme. It is normally returned after the tenancy ends, once the check-out inspection is done and any deductions are agreed. We will confirm the details with you nearer the time.

Kind regards,
Lettings team
Mare & Co
